capacity_policy: Google Drive is a bounded handoff transport/cache under the current user constraint (~15 GB), not the terminal archive. Keep only active/recent immutable packs there; do not copy a monolithic multi-industry database on every handoff. No authoritative or unreconstructable research state may exist only in a sandbox: sandbox-only files are permitted only when they are disposable caches, failed attempts, superseded intermediates, or byte-identical copies of state already persisted in Git/Drive/another durable authority.
postgres_policy: Do not transport a PostgreSQL cluster as session state. PostgreSQL remains the transactional write/ops engine and is rebuilt in an Action or other service-capable runtime when writes/leases/outbox semantics are required. Durable handoff truth is immutable source/archive bytes plus reconciled portable research packs and repository receipts.
duckdb_policy: DuckDB is the portable read/replay materialization. A fresh sandbox restores only the packs required by the current cursor, verifies outer and inner SHA-256, installs the pinned offline runtime only when the sandbox lacks a compatible DuckDB, and opens packs read-only.
terminal_archive_status: No terminal cross-session object-store archive is configured yet. Runtime Evidence execution uses content-addressed filesystem/S3 abstractions, but GitHub-hosted filesystem roots are ephemeral. Drive assets listed here are durable handoff/cache mirrors, not the terminal source of truth. A future terminal archive should preserve content-addressed raw source bytes and parser artifacts in an S3-compatible or equivalent durable object store without changing source authority semantics.
supersession_policy: Assets are immutable and append-only. Never replace bytes behind an existing Drive file id. A new pack gets a new asset id/file id and current.json/data-plane.json advance to it; older packs remain cold until explicit capacity cleanup after successor verification.
